stem: Which child with an otherwise similar acute viral upper-airway illness should have the lowest threshold for escalation because age-related physiology can reduce oxygen offload to tissues?
explanation: A 3-month-old infant is the best answer because young infants have relatively higher foetal haemoglobin, which reduces oxygen offload to tissues and warrants a lower threshold for escalation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Respiratory 3.1 Acute Respiratory Problems

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a 3-month-old infant is within the early infancy period when relatively higher foetal haemoglobin can reduce oxygen offload to tissues.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because by 10 months the infant is beyond the early period in which relatively higher foetal haemoglobin is the key concern.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because a 2-year-old child is well beyond the age range where foetal haemoglobin-related reduction in oxygen offload is most relevant.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a 6-year-old child does not have the early infancy physiology described in the stem.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a 12-year-old adolescent does not have the early infancy physiology described in the stem.
